items.title: Define the division of labor first when working in groups
items.core: It is easiest to argue about the division of labor when working in groups, so clarify the boundaries before speaking.
body: Assign tasks according to tasks rather than favors. Write clearly who will pay what and when.
Leave space for filling in, and agree on how to pick up the slack when someone falls behind.
Make a list of tasks in the first minute of the meeting, specifying the person in charge, completion time and acceptance method one by one.
Split the vague "help with PPT" into finding templates, typesetting, and proofreading to avoid missed responsibilities.
Repeat it after the division of labor: who handed in what at what time, and synchronize it to the group announcement to leave traces.

Case: The group did market research on Wednesday night. Xiaolin first listed the three responsible items in the group for data collection, PPT, and reporting, and made an appointment to check with each other on Friday. In the end no one was duplicating work and the presentation was completed on time.

items.title: Don’t let one person do it all
items.core: Long-term one-way dedication will make the relationship unbalanced.
body: When you find that the progress is concentrated on yourself, propose reassignment as soon as possible.
Speak "I need help" as a specific request rather than an emotional complaint.
When I found myself finishing up twice in a row, I immediately proposed reassignment in the group without waiting for my emotions to explode.
Describe the workload into specific items. For example, I am responsible for typesetting for three hours, and you are responsible for finding twenty pictures.
If someone is really having difficulties, they can change it to a small task, but the same person cannot be allowed to do key links for a long time.

Case: Four people in the dormitory made posters. For the first two times, Amin typed them until early in the morning. The third time she spread out the task list and asked everyone to claim the copywriting, color matching and cutting, and the final delivery was smoother.

items.title: There must be a time for return of borrowed items
items.core: Borrowing items is a turnover of trust, not a gift.
body: Indicate the purpose and return node when speaking.
Please explain the condition of use when returning it, and you will be responsible for any damage.
Take the initiative to tell the latest return time before lending it out, such as before getting off work on Friday. If you don't return it, say hello in advance.
You can take photos to record the status of your borrowed valuables. Check them in person and say thank you when you return them.
If you cannot repay on time, explain the reason and new time first, and do not wait for the other party to urge you.

Case: During the lunch break of the internship, Xiao Zhou borrowed a colleague’s charger and said on the spot that he would return it before get off work. Even after working overtime, he still sent a message to explain and brought it back the next day. His colleagues were later willing to lend him tools.

items.title: If the group disagrees, return to the goal first
items.core: Disputes are often due to different goals.
body: First confirm what you want to achieve with this assignment, and then discuss the path.
Write the differences into two options and compare costs rather than people.
If the dispute lasts for more than five minutes, write a common goal on the whiteboard and first confirm what problem everyone wants to solve.
Score the plan according to goals, such as participation, cost, and time, to reduce pure taste disputes.
Let those with different opinions express their concerns, and then merge the desirable parts into a compromise version.

Case: At the club activity planning meeting, two people debated whether to play games or give lectures. The host wrote down the goal: to let the freshmen get to know each other, and finally selected an ice-breaking game and condensed the lecture.

items.title: Don’t expose classmates’ shortcomings in public
items.core: Correction in public will make people focus on face.
body: Private reminder and public affirmation.
When it comes to principled errors, only state the facts and consequences.
When you find someone else making a mistake, use your eyes or private chat to remind them. Don’t call your name in front of the stage and say you forgot something.
If the results are affected, fill in the gaps first, and then discuss the reasons and improvements separately after the problem is over.
When correcting the content, you are correcting the subject and not the person. Use this page of data as a substitute. Why are you wrong again?

Case: During the class presentation, Xiao Chen found that one page of his data was missing. He did not say anything to his deskmate on the spot but asked him in a low voice to make up for it. After class, my deskmate took the initiative to admit and apologize, and the relationship between the two was not tense.

items.title: When asked to help, estimate one's own ability first
items.core: If you agree too quickly, you often can't do it later.
body: Ask first how much time and skills are required.
When unsure, give a clear reply time instead of a vague promise.
First ask about the deadline, workload and your available time, and then decide which step to take.
Give me a clear boundary when you can’t accept everything. For example, I can only help you organize information until nine o’clock tonight.
If you refuse, provide a feasible alternative, such as recommending tools or finding another classmate. Don’t just say you are unavailable.

Case: On Friday afternoon, a classmate asked Xiao He to help make an exhibition board. After seeing his exam review amount in the evening, he only agreed to help find pictures for half an hour. The classmate found another person to type the layout, and the display board was not delayed.

items.title: Leave a feedback after the cooperation is over
items.core: The final feedback determines whether you are willing to cooperate next time.
body: Name the specific things the other person did well.
Place suggestions for improvement in the context of next cooperation.
At the end of the cooperation, send a specific affirmation to explain which action of the other party helped the progress.
The improvement suggestions only mention one of the most critical points, and are accompanied by executable practices next time.
Thanks should be based on specific contributions. For example, the data you added last night made the report more stable and complete.

Case: After the debate competition training, the team leader sent each person two pieces of specific feedback, praising Xiao Liu for his speed in presenting evidence and reminding Xiao Lin that his speech speed was too fast. Everyone is more willing to communicate in advance the next time we form a team.

items.title: Narrow the problem down when asking for help
items.core: The more specific the problem, the easier it is for others to help.
body: Speak clearly at which step you are stuck and what you have tried.
Give the other party room to refuse.
Before asking for help, write down your stuck points, such as which steps you don’t know, what you have tried, and what kind of advice you want.
Reduce the material to one page, one question or a paragraph to reduce the cost of the other party's reply.
Give me an optional time or format. If it’s convenient, help me read it for ten minutes. It’s okay if it’s inconvenient.

Case: Xiao Wu asked his senior how to prepare for an interview. His original words were too broad and no one responded. Later, he changed it to a three-minute self-introduction and job requirements. The senior gave two suggestions for modification that night.

items.title: Don’t assume that others are available
items.core: Taking “helping you” as a matter of course is the beginning of relationship consumption.
body: Ask the other party about their current arrangements first.
Indicate approximately how much time it will take.
Before speaking, ask if it is convenient and include an estimate of how long it will take. Don’t treat the request as a notification.
Give the other party a way out when hesitating. For example, if you are busy first, I can find someone else later.
Urgent requests should state the reason for the urgency and save the other party steps, such as the files have been formatted.

Case: During the lunch break, Xiao Wang directly handed the document to his deskmate for help in printing. The deskmate was busy with homework and looked bad. Xiao Wang asked if it was convenient and made an appointment in the afternoon. His deskmate agreed and printed it more carefully.

items.title: Thank you should correspond to specific actions
items.core: A general thank you has no memory.
body: Tell me what the other person did that solved your problem.
Feedback again after the results come out.
Speak out the specific actions and results when thanking, so that the other party knows that their efforts are seen.
Avoid just sending a thank you emoji and add a sentence about the form you made which saved me half an hour.
In addition to thanking you privately, publicly thank you by name in relevant groups, but don’t exaggerate your claim of credit.

Case: After the group report, Xiao Zhao said to the classmate who helped borrow the classroom: If you confirm the projection in advance, we will save two trips. After hearing this, the other party expressed that he would be willing to take charge of the venue next time.

items.title: Returns do not have to be equivalent, but they must be timely
items.core: The accounts of the relationship are not settled at once.
body: Take the initiative to appear when the other party needs it.
Tell the other person the resources you can provide instead of waiting for him to speak.
After accepting help, try to express your feelings on the same day or the next day. If you delay thanking you for too long, it will appear perfunctory.
You can use small actions to repay, such as bringing a glass of water, helping to hold a seat, and forwarding information. There is no need to force a big gift.
When repaying the favor, state which help it corresponds to, so that the other party can feel that your kindness is truly remembered.

Case: A classmate helped Xiao Tang occupy a seat for self-study one night. The next day, he brought a bottle of water and said that the row was very quiet yesterday and helped him review steadily. The classmate laughed and said he would call again if necessary.

items.title: Don’t ask for reasons after being rejected
items.core: Asking for reasons is often a form of pressure.
body: Simple acknowledgment and then switch to other solutions.
Reserve the possibility that the other party will be willing to help in the future.
When you hear rejection, reply with a sentence of understanding. Don’t keep asking why, is it really not possible?
Leave follow-up arrangements to yourself and avoid pushing the other party into a situation where you have to explain.
If adjustments are really needed, I’ll tell you the next day and I won’t bother you until the next time is convenient. Don’t put pressure on the spot.

Case: Xiao Zheng asked a classmate to help move during the weekend, but the other party said it was inconvenient that day. Xiao Zheng only said yes, and later made an appointment with Lalahuo. He thanked the other party on Monday, and the relationship was not awkward.

items.title: Don’t make decisions for others
items.core: The limit of helping is to give options, not to choose for them.
body: List the risks and benefits you can see.
Leave the final choice to the parties involved.
List the information you can provide into options, such as cost, time, and risk, and then let the other party sort and choose.
Ask the other party about the conditions they care about most, and then explain the differences around these conditions. Don't directly say what you should do.
Explain that your suggestions are for reference only, and remind you that it is best to allow time for cooling down before confirming key decisions.

Case: My friend is hesitant to resign. I only list the pros and cons, salary and risks of staying and leaving, and let her weigh it herself. She finally chose to negotiate a job transfer first, saying afterwards that she felt more in control this way.

items.title: Big countries must respond to small matters
items.core: Failure to respond to messages is a low-cost loss of trust.
body: If you are busy, let me know when you can reply.
Always give clear answers even when you are unable to help.
When you see the message, reply first that it has been received, and then add the estimated reply time to avoid the other party guessing repeatedly while waiting.
If it is temporarily unavailable, please indicate when it will be busy, and provide an alternative contact person or next step arrangement.
Important information is confirmed by repeating events, deadlines, and responsible persons to reduce misunderstandings and missed responsibilities.

Case: My colleague Zhou Duo sent me a client’s draft revision request, but I was busy in a meeting and didn’t reply. I'll add a message tonight that I've received it, and I'll give it time tomorrow morning. The other party arranged the client accordingly and there was no delay in making an appointment.

items.title: First figure out who is the decision-maker
items.core: If you find the wrong person, no matter how much you do, you won't be able to push it away.
body: Ask who makes the decisions and who executes the process.
Leave information for both executors and decision-makers when reporting.
When taking over cross-department matters, first ask who has the final decision-making power and who only provides opinions to avoid doing it in vain.
Check the approval chain and historical emails to confirm the decision maker’s concerns, and then prepare materials according to these concerns.
Confirm the advancement nodes and feedback methods with key people. Don’t just wait for everyone in the group to express their opinions.

Case: Everyone in the project group was changing the plan. I first privately asked the team leader who made the final decision, and found out that it was the person in charge of the budget. After communicating directly with the budget sheet, the plan was approved on the same day.

items.title: Reports should bring conclusions
items.core: What superiors lack most is a sense of certainty.
body: Let’s talk about the results and next steps first, and then add the background.
List the uncertainties separately.
State the conclusion first, such as whether it can be completed on time, whether it needs to be extended, or whether option A is recommended, and then expand on the basis.
Compress the data into three parts: gap, reason, and action, so that superiors can quickly determine whether intervention is needed.
At the end, clarify the decision or support you need. Don’t let your superiors not know what to do next after listening to it.

Case: During the weekly meeting, I will first say in one sentence that this month’s goal can be achieved, and then add three risks and required support. The leader directly approves the addition, eliminating the need to repeatedly ask for reasons.

items.title: Confirm acceptance standards when accepting tasks
items.core: If the standards are unclear, rework is inevitable.
body: Ask clearly about the delivery form and time.
Repeat verbal requests into written confirmation.
When accepting a task, ask about the form of deliverables, number of words and pages, data size and deadline. It is best to write it down on the spot.
Restate the verbal requirements into a list and send it to the other party for confirmation, especially indicating what content must be included.
When encountering vague words such as as soon as possible, perfect, and good-looking, ask for a qualified example or a clear bottom line.

Case: The leader asked me to make a customer analysis report. I first confirmed the number of pages, caliber, data and submission time. It will be passed once completed according to the confirmation version, and there will be no rework due to format and indicators.

items.title: Don’t judge colleagues behind their backs
items.core: In the workplace, information will be distorted and spread.
body: Talk to the situation, not the person, and only when necessary.
Leave your opinions to those who can change the outcome.
Try to state the facts to your colleagues' opinions face to face, such as which materials were submitted late, and do not evaluate personality or ability.
When you need help, only describe the stuck points in collaboration, without making any guesses, to avoid the information becoming tainted in the retelling.
Don’t add insult to injury when you hear someone complaining. You can bring the topic back to the solution or remain silent.

Case: In the tea room, I casually said that my colleague was slow in planning. The next day, the words came to her ears and turned into "I am not capable". Later, I clarified it in person and changed it to only discuss the progress of the task.

items.title: Leave traces of your work
items.core: What has been done needs to be traceable.
body: Retain key communications in text.
Phased results are automatically synchronized.
Send a note of important decisions by email or group message, and write down the time, background, conclusion and person responsible.
After the meeting, organize the action items, including the person in charge and the deadline, and send them to the participants for confirmation.
Save the attachment version and approval screenshot, and mark the file name with the date and version to facilitate subsequent tracing.

Case: The budget of the activity I was responsible for was temporarily changed. I changed the reason, amount and approver synchronously in the group, and saved the email attachment. At the end of the month, I made a quick explanation based on the records and was not questioned.

items.title: Learn to say "I need resources"
items.core: It is not an ability, it is a risk.
body: Explain what is missing and what the consequences will be.
Give acceptable alternatives.
When you find that the workload exceeds your time or ability, explain the gap as early as possible and don’t wait until the deadline is approaching before asking for help.
When applying for resources, bring a task list, risk consequences and suggested solutions, so that the other party can easily judge whether to support it.
Clear whether you need people, data, permissions, or time, and propose minimum deliverable standards.

Case: The project had to deliver three reports at the same time. I originally wanted to work overtime to handle it, but later I explained the manpower gap and the risk of delay to my supervisor. The supervisor transferred an intern and the three reports were completed on time.

items.title: Complete the handover before resigning
items.core: The quality of the closing determines the reputation of the industry.
body: List to-do, contacts and file locations.
Allow a period of time for the receiver to ask questions.
List the ongoing items, key contacts, account permissions and risk points in advance, and hand them over according to priority.
Use documents to record operating steps and frequently asked questions, and ask the person taking over to repeat them on site to confirm understanding.
Complete written confirmation of pending matters before resigning to avoid subsequent problems coming back to you to put out the fire.

Case: Before leaving my job, I organized the account list, project progress and to-do risks, and led the successor to demonstrate each item for two weeks. After leaving my post, the other party only asked me twice for details, and the original team was not interrupted due to the handover.

items.title: Treat feedback as information instead of inappropriate evaluation
items.core: Useful data is often hidden in criticism.
body: Extract the executable points first.
You don’t have to accept the emotional part entirely.
When you hear criticism, record the specific facts first. If there is any unclear part or lack of evidence, don’t rush to defend the motive.
Divide the feedback into two categories: actionable and re-confirmation. Perform the clear parts first, and then ask about the vague parts.
Use the modified results to verify whether the feedback is valid, rather than using one evaluation to label yourself.

Case: My supervisor said that the data in my plan was too scattered. I felt aggrieved at first, but later I split my opinion into three columns: "structure, evidence, and conclusion" and revised the draft. The second version passed, and I retained the three-column inspection method.

items.title: Think clearly about the relationship costs before borrowing money
items.core: Once money is involved, there is one more variable in the relationship.
body: Ask yourself if you can afford not to pay the money back.
Write the amount and deadline in words.
Before borrowing money, confirm the purpose, amount, repayment date and source to avoid vague promises that turn into long-term disputes.
Only borrow money that you can afford to lose, and make it clear whether to write an IOU and how to transfer the money and leave a voucher.
Give a brief reason and alternative suggestions when rejecting, and do not explain repeatedly to avoid turning into bargaining.

Case: A friend temporarily borrowed 20,000 yuan for turnover. I first asked about the purpose and repayment date. After evaluation, I only borrowed 5,000 yuan and stated the deadline. He paid back the money when it was due, and the relationship did not become awkward due to pressure.

items.title: No intermediary guarantee
items.core: Guarantee is taking other people's risks to yourself.
body: Explain the principle when rejecting and do not evaluate the other party.
Provide alternative channels of information rather than credit.
Refuse to sign when faced with a guarantee request, indicating that you are not responsible for repayment by others, and avoid turning feelings into debts.
If you want to help, you can provide information verification or repayment planning, but do not mortgage, jointly guarantee or jointly borrow money.
Keep records of rejections and communications, and when the amount involved is large, consult a professional before making any commitments.

Case: A relative wanted me to guarantee a loan. After I learned about it, I found out that his income was unstable. I refused to sign and only helped him organize a repayment plan. Later, he was overdue and I was not charged with debt collection.

items.title: AA Say it in advance
items.core: Don’t talk about money until the bill arrives. The atmosphere is most likely to be awkward.
body: Confirm the sharing method before dining.
When the gap is large, take the initiative to give the opponent steps.
When sending out an invitation for a dinner date, please indicate whether it is AA, estimated per capita, and whether drinks are included. Don’t wait until you pay the bill before asking.
If someone is treating you, confirm the boundary privately in advance and don’t change it to AA temporarily after you get the bill.
Before checking out, please calculate the number of people, dishes and coupons, and write down the cost of the meal in the transfer note.

Case: A colleague made an appointment for hot pot after get off work. Before ordering, the organizer mentioned this meal in the group and everyone agreed. The bill is divided according to the number of people when checking out, no one is embarrassed, and we can make an appointment for the next time after the meal.

items.title: Don’t hide obvious risks for your friends
items.core: Really caring is not about following along.
body: Point out risks privately and give specific evidence.
Respect the other party’s final decision.
When you find that a large amount of money, health or illegal risks are involved, first clearly state the specific consequences you are worried about.
Don’t be perfunctory with “Maybe it’s okay”. Instead, list the evidence and verifiable channels and let the other party make their own judgment.
Express concern but keep boundaries, do not sign for payment on behalf of the other person, and do not hide the situation from his family on his behalf.

Case: My friend was going to invest his savings in a project recommended by an acquaintance. I thought it was risky, so I directly raised my doubts and accompanied him to check his qualifications. In the end, he withdrew the transfer.

items.title: Gifts should be based on relationship, not price
items.core: Expensive gifts will bring burdens.
body: Choose something that the other party can use.
Avoid putting pressure on the other person to reciprocate the gift.
First understand the other person’s habits and group budget, and the price of the gift should not significantly exceed the intimacy of the relationship.
Choose small things that can be used or shared, which are less burdensome than expensive but impractical things.
Avoid giving gifts with personal implications, such as jewelry and perfume, unless the relationship is clear and the other party likes it.

Case: It was a colleague’s birthday, and we all agreed that the gift budget would be within 100 yuan. I gave her her favorite books and notes, and she was very happy on the spot. Another person gave her an expensive necklace, but she was worried about returning the gift.

items.title: If the accounts are clear, the relationship will last longer
items.core: Unclear money is the easiest way to accumulate resentment.
body: Small transactions are settled promptly.
Keep records of large transactions.
Before renting together, purchasing on behalf of others, or traveling together, agree on the sharing rules, payment methods, and settlement time.
Keep screenshots or notes for each payment, and summarize it in a table at the end of the month to avoid relying solely on memory and feelings.
Report the reconciliation on the day you discover the difference in amount, and don’t let your dissatisfaction wait until the relationship becomes cold.

Case: Roommates in a shared house used a shared form to record water, electricity and daily necessities at the beginning, and reconciled the accounts every month. Half a year later, they still helped each other when moving, and there were no conflicts over money.

items.title: What is said at the dinner table will be spread out by default
items.core: Private occasions do not mean confidential occasions.
body: Do not disclose privacy, salary and evaluation to others.
Use a joke or deflect when questioned.
Don’t talk about other people’s privacy, salary, feelings, and evaluations at the dinner table. By default, everyone present may repeat it.
When you want to complain, just talk about the matter itself, without names, departments and identifiable details, to reduce the risk of communication.
If you are asked about sensitive information, say "This is not convenient to talk about" and then take the initiative to change the topic of security.

Case: During a department dinner, someone complained in a low voice that the leadership's arrangements were unfair, and even ordered specific projects; the original words reached the leadership's ears the next day, and the person involved was very passive at the meeting.

items.title: Don’t use other people’s shortcomings as a topic
items.core: The boundary of the joke is that the person involved can also laugh.
body: It is safer to make fun of yourself than to make fun of others.
Change the topic immediately when you find that the other person is uncomfortable.
Before joking, check to see if the person is really relaxed. If he is silent or reluctant, change the subject immediately.
Don’t take appearance, family, education, income, and physical condition as obstacles. These shortcomings are the most difficult to withdraw.
If you have made a mistake, apologize briefly on the spot and stop explaining. Don't use "just a joke" to continue to hit.

Case: At a colleague gathering, someone repeatedly teased the newcomer about his accent. The newcomer lowered his head and said nothing, and other colleagues could not laugh. After that, he rarely attended department dinners.

items.title: It is better to respect your choice than to persuade you to drink
items.core: Take it as a personal decision whether to drink or not.
body: Offer alternative drinks.
There is no need to put pressure with face-saving words.
Immediately accept when the other party says he doesn’t want to drink. Don’t ask for the reason. You can offer tea, drinks or non-alcoholic drinks instead.
Don’t put pressure on people by saying, “If you don’t drink, you won’t give face.” Separate the amount of alcohol from friendship and willingness to cooperate.
Organize a variety of drinks before the meal, and take care of people with dietary restrictions, medication and driving when ordering.

Case: At a client dinner, a colleague said he had a bad stomach and only drank tea. No one continued to persuade him, so the client also drank tea. Everyone talked about the project more smoothly, and the follow-up cooperation progressed smoothly.

items.title: Restate the conflict first and then respond
items.core: People cannot listen to reason when they are misunderstood.
body: First tell what you understand the other person’s meaning.
State your facts and feelings again.
Before responding, restate the other party’s appeal in your own words, and then explain your position after confirming it is correct.
When retelling, tell only facts and feelings, without adding ridicule, speculation, or labeling the other person.
When the other party is emotional, pause for ten minutes and agree on a time to continue the conversation to avoid getting more and more angry.

Case: Roommates quarreled over the temperature of the air conditioner. One party first said, "You think it's too cold at night and want to raise the temperature by two degrees." The other party's mood calmed down, and then they negotiated a time plan.

items.title: Do not deal with private conflicts in the group
items.core: Public occasions will make it difficult for both parties to step down.
body: Go to one-to-one communication.
Only conclusions and follow-up arrangements are left in the group.
Private disputes should be discussed privately or scheduled for an interview first, and should not be discussed in a group with leaders and bystanders.
Only necessary facts and progress are synchronized in the group, and emotional judgments, old accounts, and personal evaluations are not written.
If conflicts affect work, invite relevant people to hold a short meeting to clarify responsibilities and next steps, and there will be no public trial.

Case: Two colleagues argued in the department group over work schedules and settled old scores with each other. Other colleagues were forced to watch. In the end, the supervisor mediated privately and reiterated the group rules.

items.title: You don’t have to say anything about your privacy when asked
items.core: The obligation to answer does not equal the right to ask questions.
body: Give me a fixed statement that won’t hurt anyone.
It is not necessary to explain the reason for rejection.
When faced with questions such as salary, age, relationship, fertility, etc., you can end the questioning with a vague answer.
When refusing, speak calmly and do not need to explain too much. The more you explain, the easier it will be for you to continue questioning.
For people who repeatedly inquire, first set boundaries and then change the topic: "Let's not talk about this for now, what have you been busy with recently?"

Case: At a relatives gathering, my cousin asked about salary and rent. I smiled and said, "I have enough to live on, and I won't consider changing it for the time being." Then I asked her about her travel plans, and the atmosphere was not tense.

items.title: Be considerate of the host’s feelings when leaving the table
items.core: It is safer to explain in advance than to disappear suddenly.
body: Explain the reason and thank you.
Add a greeting later.
When you need to leave early, please explain the reason and departure time to the host first, and do not make a loud announcement that affects the entire audience.
Nod to your tablemates before leaving, and lower your voice to avoid interrupting the ongoing chat.
If you are an invited core guest, try to wait until the main course and toast are over, and then politely leave.

Case: Halfway through a friend’s family dinner, I left beforehand. I told the host alone in advance and explained the reason, and helped put away the wine glasses before leaving. The host was not embarrassed.

items.title: Remember the little things that others have mentioned
items.core: Details are the lowest cost to care about.
body: Write down the other person’s taboos and schedule.
Next time, take the initiative to mention it and don’t deliberately take credit.
When you hear the other person mention allergies, dietary restrictions, anniversaries, or to-do items, immediately write them down in your phone notes.
The next time we meet, take the initiative to follow up with "How was the interview we talked about last time?", which will make people take it more seriously than just casual greetings.
Remember that small things do not mean prying, they are only used to care and help, and do not mention the other person's difficulties in public.

Case: My friend said last month that she wanted to learn how to swim. When I passed by a bookstore and saw the introductory manual, I took a photo and sent it to her. She said she was very surprised because it was just a casual mention.

items.title: Boundaries should be stated when the relationship is good
items.core: Wait until the conflict breaks out, and it becomes an accusation.
body: When you are calm, explain how you can help.
Replace "You can't..." with "I can...".
Find a time when both parties are relaxed, and use "I am more accustomed to..." to explain your schedule, privacy, or how you spend money.
Start by practicing small, low-risk things, such as not accepting temporary requests, and observe whether the other party can respond smoothly.
Set the boundaries into specific rules: after what time no messages will be returned, which items cannot be borrowed, and how to suspend communication after crossing the boundary.

Case: Xiao Zhang has always had a good relationship with his friends. During a casual chat, he calmly mentioned that he did not like being arbitrarily borrowed money, and his friend expressed understanding. Later, when a friend encountered an emergency, he turned to him for advice instead of borrowing money. The boundaries between the two were clear, and the relationship became easier and longer lasting.

items.title: Allow others to say no
items.core: Rejection does not mean denying you.
body: Allow an escape route when making a request.
Don’t ask or care after the other party refuses.
After hearing "inconvenient", reply "ok" first, and don't ask for the reason immediately, so as to save the other party the cost of explanation.
When inviting colleagues to dinner, prepare a list of candidates. If one person declines the invitation, you can directly ask others.
First determine whether it is a matter of time, physical strength or preference. Don’t elevate a single rejection to an overall evaluation.

Case: Before the department team building, Xiao Li asked his colleagues if they could come to help move supplies on Sunday. The colleagues said they would accompany his father for a review. Xiao Li said, "It doesn't matter, you take care of your family first" and found two other people to complete the task. As a result, colleagues later took the initiative to design the exhibition boards.

items.title: Give alternatives when rejecting
items.core: Hard rejection is easy to hurt, but giving a path is more likely to be accepted.
body: Explain what you can’t do.
Recommend another feasible method.
First say the part that you cannot agree to, and then add "What I can do is..." to give the other party the next step to take.
When a colleague asks you to take over the shift, you can reply "Not tonight, you can change the shift on Wednesday, or I can ask Xiao Li for you."
Alternatives should be specific to time, people, or resources, and avoid dangling responses like “we’ll talk about it later.”

Case: A colleague temporarily asked Amin to do a weekly report for him. Amin was rushing to work on a client project. She said she couldn't take it tonight, but she could send him a template tomorrow morning and teach him for ten minutes. The colleague finished it on her own and thanked her for not telling her the truth.

items.title: Relationships are maintained by predictability
items.core: Hot and cold consumes most trust.
body: Keep your promises on time.
State changes are explained in advance.
A fixed contact rhythm, such as a phone call once a week and a meeting once a month, so that the other party does not have to guess whether you are there or not.
Report in advance when you work overtime temporarily or feel depressed, and explain how long it will take to resume contact, so as to reduce the other party's anxiety about waiting.
The response speed does not have to be seconds, but it should be as stable as possible; when you are busy, just say "I'll take a closer look later" first, and don't lose the enthusiasm for a while.

Case: Xiao Li found that his partner's recent replies to messages have been fast and slow, sometimes passionate and intimate, and sometimes suddenly cold. He repeatedly guessed the other party's attitude, felt exhausted, and gradually lost trust. It wasn't until the two had a frank communication that they realized it was work pressure that caused mood swings, not a deterioration of their relationship.

items.title: Don’t bind others with a sense of debt
items.core: Relationships maintained by guilt are not strong.
body: Do not mention it repeatedly when helping.
Don’t regard past efforts as bargaining chips.
Don’t ask for help again and again after you’ve helped, especially when the other party can’t satisfy you, don’t turn old things into bargaining chips.
When asking for help, add the sentence "just say if it's inconvenient", and explain in advance the approximate time and difficulty.
If you agree only because you are afraid of sorry for the other person, pause first and confirm whether you are really willing before deciding whether to continue.

Case: An old classmate repeatedly said "I helped you last time" and asked Xiao Zhou to line up for her to grab a ticket. After Xiao Zhou helped her buy the ticket, he made it clear that he could only help her so far. Although the other party was unhappy, he rarely used old things to put pressure again.

items.title: Intimacy does not mean no distance
items.core: No matter how close the relationship is, personal space is needed.
body: Respect each other’s alone time.
Feel free to contact us at any time without request.
Allow each other a fixed period of time alone, such as two hours a week for each to do their own thing, and there is no requirement to report at any time.
Ask a question before checking your phone, digging through packages, or collecting messages on your behalf. The default permission is limited to the scope stated in advance.
Close people can also have independent friends and accounts. They don’t have to share everything, but they still need to explain important arrangements in advance.

Case: A couple will set aside one hour of alone time every day. The husband reads a book and the wife writes a diary. At first, my wife felt alienated, but later found that this time made each other more relaxed, and they cherished the time together more. The relationship was close while maintaining personal space.

items.title: Regular review of relationship status
items.core: Long-term relationships need to be maintained rather than indulged.
body: Ask each other if they are feeling well lately.
Solve small problems when you are young.
Set aside quiet time every three months to talk about recent interactions that have been comfortable and arrangements that have been stressful for each other.
When reviewing, give a specific incident in each case. Instead of starting with "you always", focus on how to adjust next time.
Write conclusions into enforceable agreements, such as frequency of contact, budget for gatherings, and how long to pause in case of conflict.

Case: Lao Chen and his old classmate have not seen each other for many years, and their relationship has gradually faded. During a gathering, they frankly communicated about changes in their lives, re-understood each other's current situation, and agreed to contact each other regularly. This review allowed the two to find a tacit understanding and their friendship continued.

items.title: Ending a relationship should be dignified
items.core: The ending method will affect each other's memory of the relationship.
body: Explain why you cannot continue.
No personal evaluation.
Choose a private and unprompted occasion to explain your decision. Tell the conclusion first, and then give the other party time to ask questions and digest.
Only describe the differences and reasons for the inability to continue. Do not settle old scores or involve a third party to judge who is right and who is wrong.
Make a clear list of account numbers, property, common items, and notifications, and agree on a processing time limit to avoid repeated hassles in the future.

Case: Postgraduate entrance examination roommates decided not to share the same apartment due to work and rest conflicts. Before moving out, they invited each other to dinner, paid the deposit and left cleaning tools. Although the two have little contact, they can still say hello naturally when they meet.

items.title: Punctuality is the most basic form of respect
items.core: Being late conveys the message that "my time is more important."
body: Confirm the route and transportation time in advance.
Inform us in advance if you may be late.
Before going out, reserve time according to the worst traffic conditions on the map. Arrive ten minutes early for important appointments, which can buffer you from finding your way.
If you expect to be late for more than ten minutes, send a message explaining the reason and new time first, and don't let the other party wait indefinitely.
Those who are often late can set their alarm clock fifteen minutes in advance and pack their preparations the night before.

Case: The customer made an appointment to see the sample clothes at ten o'clock in the morning, and the shopkeeper prepared tea and sample clothes ten minutes in advance. When the customer arrives on time, he tries it on and places an order directly, saying, "You can worry less here and don't have to wait for anyone."

items.title: Give information to both parties when introducing others
items.core: It is difficult to start a conversation by only giving names.
body: Give a background for each sentence.
Give the topic back to them.
When introducing, state your name, current job or interests, and add a common topic that both parties may understand.
Address the more senior or older person first before introducing the other person to avoid making the address seem casual.
When it comes to sensitive information such as marriage, income, health, etc., obtain the consent of the person first and do not break the ice with personal matters.

Case: During the industry coffee break, the host only said, "This is Mr. Wang and Teacher Chen", and the two nodded awkwardly. A friend next to me added, "Mr. Wang is responsible for the catering supply chain, and Teacher Chen writes consumer reports," and they quickly started talking about cooperation.

items.title: Remembering names is more useful than remembering titles
items.core: Being remembered is the most basic thing to be seen.
body: Repeat it on the spot to confirm.
Take the initiative to greet me when you meet again.
After hearing the name, immediately repeat it: "Is this Zhang Min?" and then naturally call it once or twice during the conversation.
Binding names and characteristics into memory, such as "Zhang Min who wears glasses" or "Chen Chen who works as a designer", is more reliable than remembering the position.
When you turn around and forget your name, don't guess. It's safer to just say "Sorry, I didn't remember it well. Can you say it again?"

Case: Xiao Wang was called by his first name by his boss at a meeting, instead of just his position. He instantly felt respected and valued. After that, he took the initiative to remember the names of his colleagues. The team atmosphere was obviously more harmonious and the communication efficiency was also improved.

items.title: Visits must be arranged in advance
items.core: Sudden visits can easily disrupt other people's arrangements.
body: State the purpose and estimated duration.
Confirm if it is convenient upon arrival.
Ask at least one day in advance, "Is this convenient?" and state the number of visitors, their purpose, and how long they expect to stay.
Try not to come to your door unexpectedly during holidays, meals and late at night. Send a message first to confirm whether the other party has arranged family matters.
If the other party says it's inconvenient, change the appointment to a specific time. Don't wait at the door or use "just come in five minutes" to pressure you.

Case: On the weekend afternoon, Xiao Zheng knocked on the door of his aunt's house with fruit without saying hello, just in time to catch up with his cousin's online class. My aunt welcomed me but kept checking the time. Xiao Zheng later sent a message to make an appointment, and the conversation became more enjoyable.

items.title: Messages are layered by occasion
items.core: Not everything is suitable for instant messaging.
body: Use the phone for emergencies.
Leave traces of complex matters in words.

For emergency work, use the phone to confirm whether the other party is convenient, and then use group messages to synchronize conclusions. Don’t treat group chats as if everyone is online at all times.
For details involving privacy, performance or emotions, use one-on-one communication instead to avoid leaving embarrassing records in the group.
Non-urgent matters should be posted during working hours, with the title clearly stating the topic, deadline, and who needs to respond to reduce repeated questioning.

Case: At 11 o'clock on Friday night, the team leader sent the contract modification and three voice messages to the department group in succession, and many people had already taken a break. The next day, he switched to email to list the changes, and only reminded to check them in the work group, so the implementation was smoother.

items.title: Public praise, private reminders
items.core: This applies to almost all relationships.
body: Be specific in your praise.
Reminder is only for the parties concerned.
When praising, state the specific behavior and impact, such as "He checked the list in advance so that there was no queue for sign-in." Don't make general exaggerations.
Make sure the environment is private before reminding, talk about the facts and consequences one-on-one, and do not go over old scores or compare others in public.
Add a sentence of support after the reminder, such as "Do you need me to help you change the template?" so that the other party will regard the correction as an improvement rather than a punishment.

Case: At the regular meeting, the supervisor praised Xiao Tang for organizing his after-sales skills into a table, and everyone applauded. After the meeting, he separately pointed out two errors in writing prices, and Xiao Tang corrected them and added notes on the same day.

items.title: Don’t ask for attention when others are busy
items.core: If the timing is wrong, no matter how good the content is, it will be ineffective.
body: Observe the opponent's current rhythm.
Change a more suitable time.
Observe the other person's status first. If the other person is in a meeting, on the road, or taking care of his family, say "I'll see you after I'm done" first, and don't send a series of messages.
Organize the content you want to share into one paragraph and write "No need to rush to reply", which not only expresses your feelings but also reduces the pressure on the other party.
If you are really in an emergency, ask "Is it convenient now?" If it's not convenient, make an appointment. Don't use your emotions to test whether the other person cares.

Case: On the day of her daughter’s kindergarten performance, her mother was helping her change clothes backstage, and Xiao Chen sent ten photos in a row asking for praise. My mother didn’t reply until she finished her work in the evening, sending a perfunctory emoji. The next day, Xiao Chen changed the post during lunch break and received a serious response.

items.title: Accept good intentions and respond
items.core: Relation needs to flow in both directions.
body: Speak clearly about what you feel.
Give back when appropriate.
Express specific thanks on the same day after receiving a meal, gift or help, and explain what made you labor-saving or happy. Don’t just reply with an emoticon.

The return gift does not have to be of equal value. Choose a small item or action that the other party can use, such as bringing fruit, helping to pick up express delivery, or buying a cup of tea in return.
Set boundaries for continued kindness. After thanking you, you can say "I'll do it this time" to avoid letting the other person become the default caregiver.

Case: The neighbor’s aunt gave soup to Xiao He who worked overtime for two consecutive days. Xiao He gave back a box of low-sugar snacks on the third day and washed the empty bowls and sent them back. Auntie said that it will be more fun to deliver soup in the future because it is no longer a one-sided worry.

items.title: Seriously say goodbye when leaving
items.core: The final impression often determines the next meeting.
body: Thanks for the specific arrangement.
Express your desire to see you again.
Before getting up, put away your cell phone, address the person and explain the reason for leaving, such as "I have an early shift tomorrow, I'll leave first." Don't disappear suddenly.
Thank you for a specific arrangement when saying goodbye, such as "This store is well chosen", so that the other party feels that your intentions are seen.
If there is a follow-up, do what you say, such as "send a message when you get home" or "I'll invite you next time." Don't make casual promises just to be polite.

Case: When friends were finishing up at a dinner party, Xiao Lin kept his head down while scrolling through his cell phone, and just said "hmm" before leaving. My cousin felt left out. The next time he got up and said it was morning, thanked him for the reception, and sent it to the door, his cousin said he would make an appointment next time.

items.title: Do not forcefully bring the relationship closer
items.core: Excessive enthusiasm will make people retreat.
body: Advance according to the opponent's rhythm.
Use "Let's get together next time" like an invitation rather than an arrangement.
First observe whether the other party is willing to chat. The topic will stay on the content he actively mentioned without asking for privacy.
Start from work intersections or common scenes, such as projects, lunch time, and nearby conveniences.
For invitations, use rejectable expressions such as "Let's get together when you have time." If the other party declines, the distance will immediately return to normal.

Case: A new colleague came to the department. During the lunch break, Xiao Li kept asking about her marriage and hometown, and even dragged her into the department group for a private chat. She only responded briefly, avoided Xiao Li during lunch, and became polite in her cooperation.

items.title: Speak less jokes in formal situations
items.core: Humor needs a common context.
body: Keep neutral expressions when in doubt.
Leave the jokes to those you know well.
Formal reports give priority to facts, data and conclusions. Humor is limited to self-deprecation and does not make fun of others or the system.
It is better not to use it when you are not sure whether the audience is familiar with the meme, especially in cross-department, cross-customer, and cross-age situations.
If the joke goes unanswered, go back to the agenda immediately and say, "Let's move on to the next item." Don't explain the punch line again.

Case: At the customer acceptance meeting, the speaker used internet memes to ridicule Party A’s process at the beginning, thinking it could liven up the atmosphere. The client just laughed awkwardly, and there were obviously fewer follow-up questions, making the meeting atmosphere more tense.

items.title: Let’s talk about the conclusion first, then the reasons
items.core: Information density determines communication efficiency.
body: The first sentence is for judgment.
Supplementary evidence and examples will follow.
In the first sentence, give a conclusion or decision, such as "can do", "can't do", and "it is recommended to choose A".
Keep your reasons to no more than three, sort them by importance, and avoid putting background details at the front.
When you need the other party to take action, write the deadline and responsible person after the conclusion to facilitate direct execution.

Case: Before the project review on Friday, the team leader first wrote in the group "delivery will be delayed for three days and will be resubmitted on Wednesday", and then listed test obstruction and remediation arrangements. The customer immediately adjusted the acceptance time, and the team received a dozen inquiries.

items.title: Write the request into an executable item
items.core: A vague request equals no request.
body: Write clearly what you want to do and when you want to do it.
Indicate priority.
Write clearly who will do it, what will be done, and when it will be completed. Avoid just saying "take a look" and "follow up."
Give the file link, page number or data location together to reduce the cost of the other party's own search and judgment.
Explain the delivery standards, such as giving conclusions, listing risks, and modifying the copy, instead of just saying "give some opinions" in general.

Case: Xiao Zhou only said in the group, "Please help me take a look at the plan." No one responded for two days. Later, he changed it to "Please Zhang San to read the budget on page 2 before leaving get off work today and mark the unreasonable items." Zhang San gave three feedback comments that day.

items.title: Restate the confirmation to avoid misunderstanding
items.core: The cost of confirmation is much lower than the cost of rework.
body: Repeat it in your own words.
List the points of disagreement separately.
After receiving the task, state the time, place, objects and deliverables to give the other party a chance to correct them on the spot.
When encountering vague words such as "as soon as possible" and "old place", ask for specific dates and specific places.
The confirmation result is sent back to the group or document visible to both parties in text, and subsequent execution is based on this record.

Case: A colleague asked Xiao Wang to make an appointment with a client, and only said, "Let's meet next Wednesday." Xiao Wang repeated, "We will have a video conference at three o'clock next Wednesday afternoon to only confirm the progress of the contract, right?" A colleague discovered that the time should be Thursday and changed it promptly.

items.title: Speech at the meeting should be short and point-of-view
items.core: It is easy to lose attention if you make a long foreshadowing.
body: One idea with one example.
Leave the details until after the meeting.
Speak out your judgment within thirty seconds, such as "It is recommended to do it", "It is not recommended to do it", "We still need data".
A speech should only focus on one point of view, and the background material should be supplemented with at most one or two key facts.
Close the next step at the end, such as "Please confirm whether to extend" or "Who needs to fill in the data and when".

Case: During the regular product meeting, Xiao Li spoke about the background for two minutes before explaining his demands. The host interrupted him. Xiao Wang then said, "It is recommended to postpone the launch due to the increase in payment failure rate and customer service complaints" and immediately entered into decision-making discussions.

items.title: Objections must be addressed
items.core: Replace "I don't agree with you" with "This plan has risks."
body: Give verifiable reasons.
Attach your alternative.
First describe the specific problems in the solution, and then provide evidence, such as historical data, customer feedback or test records.
Avoid using expressions such as "you always" and "you don't understand" to evaluate personality, and instead discuss plans and results.
After objecting, add an executable alternative action, such as increasing the buffer period, reducing the scope, or conducting a pilot first.

Case: During the scheduling review, Xiao Zhang wanted to say "You underestimated the workload again", but changed it on the spot to "This schedule misses interface joint debugging, and it will be two days longer in the past." The person in charge accepted the reminder and postponed the launch date.

items.title: Written communication must be read independently
items.core: and it can be considered clear if it is still valid without context.
body: Add background and conclusion.
Avoid abbreviations that only the person involved will understand.
Write the time, object, file name, and modification location in full. It is assumed that the reader has not participated in the previous discussion.
In important emails, write the conclusion first, then add the necessary background, and finally list the action items and deadlines.
The attachment name contains the project, version and date, and the text description shall be based on which version shall be used to avoid confusion.

Case: Someone in the project group said, "Change that table as mentioned last time." The new colleague couldn't understand it at all. Later, he rewritten it as "Please change the third column of the June quotation table to unify the tax-included price and send it back before noon tomorrow." The other party completed it in one go.

items.title: Don’t wait to be asked when synchronizing progress
items.core: Active synchronization can reduce a lot of questioning.
body: Fixed cadence for short updates.
Risks are exposed in advance.
Set a fixed synchronization rhythm, such as a sentence of progress in daily stand-up meetings, or status updates in the group every two days.
On the day you get stuck, explain what is missing, which step will be affected, and who needs support. Don’t delay until the deadline.
Write clearly completed, next steps and risks when synchronizing, so that relevant people do not have to ask repeatedly.

Case: During the production of event posters, the designer waited for two days for the brand logo and did not say anything until the night before it was launched. Later, he sent a message about progress and stuck points every day, and the missing materials were coordinated and resolved on the same day.

items.title: Allow time window for feedback
items.core: It may not be digested on the spot.
body: The explanation can be discussed later.
Agree a time for response.
For major or negative feedback, don’t force the other party to respond on the spot. Instead, first say, “Let’s digest it and we’ll talk tomorrow.”
Agree on a specific feedback time window, such as supplementary comments within 24 hours, to avoid infinite delays in feedback.
Send background material or a list of questions ahead of time to give the other party time to compile facts and alternatives.

Case: During the department review meeting, the supervisor asked the newcomer to evaluate the plan on the spot. The newcomer was nervous and only said "very good". The supervisor instead distributed materials after the meeting and made an appointment to chat alone the next day. The newcomer raised two key questions.

items.title: At home, talk about facts before talking about feelings
items.core: Discussions between stories can easily turn into quarrels.
body: First describe what happened.
Let’s talk about the feelings brought about by this incident.
First talk about the facts that can be confirmed, such as time, number of times, specific actions, without drawing conclusions or characterization first.
Use "I feel" to express emotions to avoid directly judging the other party's motives as indifference or intentionality.
Finally make an executable request, such as reporting half an hour in advance or making up family time on the weekend.

Case: The husband said he would work overtime after the food was cold for two consecutive days. The wife first asked, "Don't you care about home?" and the two quarreled. Later, she changed to stating the facts and feelings of loss, and then her husband explained the situation and agreed to report it in advance.

items.title: Not saying "you always"
items.core: Full name Judgment will immediately trigger defensiveness.
body: Replace it with what happened specifically this time.
State the requirements into actionable actions.
Replace "you always" with the actual fact, such as "the dishes were not washed tonight", and it will be more difficult for the other party to refute.
Only discuss the matter at hand, do not go over old scores, and do not extend to personality, habits or character evaluation.
After saying the behavior, give the next action directly, such as "put the laundry basket back" or "put the desk away before going to bed."

Case: The child threw two socks on the sofa. The mother blurted out, "You are always so sloppy." The child immediately talked back. She changed it to "The socks on the sofa were confiscated today", and the child was silent for a while before putting them in the laundry basket.

items.title: Intimacy also requires consent
items.core: Default does not replace explicitness.
body: Important decisions must be confirmed by both parties.
Respect the other person’s right to change their mind at any time.
When it comes to physical contact, mobile phone privacy or social accounts, first confirm "Is it okay now" with one sentence, and get a clear response before taking action.
When the other party hesitates, remains silent, or changes the topic, treat it as a temporary disagreement. Stop what you are doing first, and then say that you can change your mind at any time.

I also take the initiative to clarify the boundaries, such as "I don't want to be dragged to meet friends temporarily", so that the other party knows how to arrange it so as not to cross the boundaries.

Case: My partner wanted to check the chat history on Xiao Min’s mobile phone, and he had taken her cup without asking before. This time he asked first, "Can I take a look?" Xiao Min said she felt uncomfortable, so he immediately stopped and apologized. Afterwards, she was more willing to take the initiative to explain her boundaries.

items.title: The division of housework must be visible
items.core: Invisible labor is most easily ignored.
body: Make a list and frequency.
Regular review of whether it is fair.
Make a list of weekly chores, indicating frequency, estimated time, and person to perform them, to avoid arguments based solely on "I'm tired today."

Tick the box on the shared form or the refrigerator whiteboard immediately after completing it, and only use ten minutes on the weekend to check the omissions and adjust the schedule for the next week.
Include invisible labor, such as recording daily necessities, making maintenance appointments, arranging physical examinations, and interpersonal relationships. Don’t default to one person.

Case: Xiao Zhou and his partner often quarrel over housework. The two of them wrote down cooking, washing dishes, taking out the trash, buying diapers and making cleaning appointments on a shared list, and whoever completed it checked the boxes. After a week, there were less disputes, and each other saw each other's efforts.

items.title: Accept the difference in rhythm when communicating with parents
items.core: Their experiences come from different environments.
body: Understand the worry first, then explain the choice.
Persuade with results rather than arguments.
Reiterating your parents' concerns first, such as "You are worried about my unstable income," and then expressing your decision can significantly reduce the sense of confrontation.

Major decisions are discussed in two or three times. First, the background, then the preparations, and finally the results. Give them time to digest rather than forcing them to express their stance all at once.
Replace abstract arguments with specific numbers and timetables, such as deposits, trial periods, project cycles and social security payment methods, so that they can see the basis.

Case: Xiao Lin wanted to resign from a state-owned enterprise to do design, but his mother objected for a week in a row. He did not argue immediately, but first listened to her worries about social security and stability, and then paid her salary and three-month project plan; after a month, his mother stopped urging him to turn back every day.

items.title: There must be repair actions after conflict
items.core: No cold war is the bottom line.
body: Speak clearly about what you care about.
Use concrete actions to express your willingness to continue.
After the argument, do a low-threshold repair action first, such as pouring a glass of water or saying "I still care about us". Don't wait for the other party to admit defeat first.
If emotions are too high, clearly agree on a time to calm down before talking again, and make the pause clear to avoid letting silence turn into a long-term cold war.
When re-communicating, only talk about your feelings and next steps, do not go over old scores, and do not ask the other party to admit all responsibilities on the spot.

Case: Aning and his partner quarreled late into the night over travel arrangements, and neither of them spoke the next day. In the evening, he bought her favorite milk tea and said, "I spoke too harshly last night." Then they rescheduled their schedule together and resumed normal communication that night.

items.title: Research the person before submitting
items.core: Generic resumes have the lowest response rate.
body: Align experience with job requirements.
Prepare a question that explains your motivation.
Read the job description before submitting, circle the three core competencies, and move the most matching experience to the first half of the resume page and the first item of project experience.
Check the company’s recent products, news, and competitive products, and write a specific observation in your cover letter to prove that you are not copying templates in bulk.
Change the project results into indicators familiar to the other party, such as conversion rate, retention rate, cost reduction and delivery cycle, so that the value can be seen at a glance.

Case: Xiao He initially submitted thirty resumes to the group and received only one reply. Later, he spent an hour checking the company's products and recruitment requirements, changed the course project to data analysis experience related to the position, and specified the time when he could join; he got two interviews within a week.

items.title: During the interview, talk about the process, not just the results
items.core: The other party wants to know how you did it.
body: Explain the constraints and choices at the time.
Give verifiable details.
Use the structure of "background-goal-action-result-review" to answer. First talk about the constraints, and then talk about why you chose this way.
Prepare two key decision-making points, explain what plans were available at the time, what was abandoned, and what the basis was, so that the other party can see the judgment process.
Try to present the results in numbers, and add a sentence to correct the failure, such as how to change the copy and channels after the first round of low conversions.

Case: When asked about event planning during the interview, Xiao Chen did not just talk about "adding three thousand new users", but also talked about how to break down the goals, choose social channels, do two versions of copywriting tests, and review the conversion; the interviewer asked for details and gave an opportunity to meet again on the spot.

items.title: Understand the range before negotiating salary
items.core: Information gaps will directly turn into losses.
body: Understand the market level through public channels.
Give educated expectations rather than random quotes.
Check recruitment platforms, peer groups and acquaintances before the interview, and record the lowest, common and highest quotes for the same position in the same city to form a psychological range.
When reporting expectations, give a well-founded range and explain that it comes from job responsibilities, skill requirements and market research. Do not report the bottom line separately.
Also ask about performance bonuses, subsidies, salary adjustment points and probation period ratios to avoid looking only at monthly salary and ignoring actual annual income.

Case: Xiao Wu was nervous when he got the offer. HR asked him about his expected salary. He said "anything is fine", but in the end he only got 14k. Later, he found out that the average salary for the same position was 18-22k. The next time he negotiated with the research range, he finally settled on 19k.

items.title: Focus on observation in the first two weeks of joining the company
items.core: First figure out the interpersonal and work rhythm.
body: Ask more about the process and draw less conclusions.
Document key people and decision paths.
Record who is leading the conclusions and who is responsible for execution in the daily meetings, and spend two to three days sorting out the actual power and collaboration relationships of the team.
Pay attention to the way tasks are assigned, whether it is a written clear request or a verbal vague assignment, and record the real decision-maker from taking over to delivery confirmation.

Observe colleagues’ reactions to unexpected problems, whether they wait for instructions or take the initiative to try and make mistakes, and judge whether the company encourages innovation or emphasizes process compliance.

Case: Newcomer Xiao Tang did not rush to criticize the process in the first two weeks of joining the company. Instead, he recorded the decision-making chain of the meeting, file storage location, and colleagues’ work and rest. Only in the third week did he know that the project leader wanted to confirm it privately before the meeting, so the proposal was approved in one go.

items.title: Treat the probation period as a two-way choice
items.core: You are also evaluating the other party.
body: Record the gap between promises and fulfillment.
Stop losses as soon as possible when a fundamental mismatch is discovered.
Check whether the first project assigned to you is a core business or a peripheral business, and determine the company's willingness to train you and its true positioning.

Pay attention to the leadership feedback method, whether it is to say "optimize it again" or to clearly point out the problem, and evaluate whether your immediate superior is willing to invest time to help you grow.
Proactively inquire about overtime frequency and compensation status, and use specific implementation rules rather than verbal promises to measure work intensity and system integrity.

Case: During the probation period, Xiao He discovered that the team had been working overtime for a long time and the training promised by the instructor had not been fulfilled. He recorded tasks and feedback, interviewed other companies at the same time, and left politely after expiration, without dragging the probation period into a waste.

items.title: Reason for leaving the job remains neutral
items.core: The industry is small and evaluations will spread.
body: Talk about development direction, not personnel conflicts.
Leave gratitude to specific people.
Uniformly use "adjustment of personal career development direction" as the external caliber, and avoid involving salary, interpersonal conflicts or specific incident details.
If you are asked repeatedly, just state objective facts such as "the team structure has been adjusted and my position has been merged." Do not evaluate the ability of the previous company or anyone.
When bidding farewell in a resignation email or work group, simply thank you for your cooperation and wish you well. Do not take the opportunity to express emotions or hint at internal problems.

Case: Xiao Xu resigned due to the chaotic division of labor in the team. During the interview, he did not criticize his supervisor by name. He only said that he hoped to shift to a clearer business direction and thanked him for his half-year training. Later, the former company gave a positive review.

items.title: Maintain minimal contact after separation
items.core: Former colleagues are long-term resources.
body: Keep greetings at reasonable times.
Do not ask for help beyond the scope of the relationship.
When adding former colleagues on professional platforms such as LinkedIn, include the name of a specific project that they have worked with to help them quickly recall shared memories.
Send short blessings that are not sent in bulk on major holidays, avoid sales or job search messages, and maintain a pure, low-pressure emotional connection.

If a former colleague asks about an industry issue that you are good at, tell him everything he knows without asking for immediate returns. A long-term and reliable persona is more valuable than frequent pleasantries.

Case: Xiao Liu sent a brief thank you to his three partners on the day he resigned, and then only sent holiday greetings. Half a year later, a former colleague thought of a position that suited her and proactively forwarded the recruitment information, and she successfully got an interview.

items.title: Every experience must leave something reusable
items.core: Turn work into ability, not consumption.
body: Organize the results that can be displayed.
Record the pitfalls and solutions.
Every time you finish a project, spend half an hour writing a "decision review": why you made the choice you did, what pitfalls you stepped into, and how to improve next time.
Organize commonly used processes, templates, and sayings into a personal document library to ensure that they can be legally taken away and continuously reused when you leave your job.

Regularly classify the projects you have done according to "capability labels", such as "cross-department promotion" and "crisis management", so that you can have ready-made materials for the next interview.

Case: Xiao Zhao worked as an event operator for two years. Before leaving, he sorted out the supplier list, review template, registration conversion data table and risk list. After changing jobs, she directly reused these methods and completed large-scale activities independently in the first month.
